Genopets is developed by a studio backed by Pantera Capital and operates a consumer mobile/web game rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Nebex
providers.description: Nebex operates Nebra Exchange, an exchange platform for the global space economy that connects commercial space suppliers, sovereign buyers such as governments and space agencies, and financial institutions. The platform aims to standardize space-commerce infrastructure so demand can find supply faster, workflows can be coordinated across multilateral participants, and capital can participate through transparent structures, facilitating complex transactions from demand to delivery including sourcing, coordination, and settlement. Founded by Tejpaul Bhatia (CEO) and Anand Subramanian (COO), both formerly of Axiom Space, Nebex is backed by GV. The company currently offers early, invite-based access to the Nebra Exchange platform and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK program.

providers.name: OnePay
providers.description: OnePay is a Walmart-backed financial technology company that delivers mobile banking and money services through a single consumer app, with banking provided by Coastal Community Bank or Lead Bank (Members FDIC). The app bundles everyday checking and high-yield savings, a Credit Builder loan and credit score monitoring, the OnePay CashRewards Mastercard credit card, buy-now-pay-later (OnePay Later, powered by Klarna/WebBank), a digital wallet, commission-free stock and ETF investing (cleared by DriveWealth), crypto buying (powered by Zero Hash), free tax filing, global transfers (powered by MoneyGram), and cash back tied to Walmart. Originally launched as ONE (One Finance), OnePay is backed by Ribbit Capital and Walmart. It operates a gated developer/partner surface at developer.onepay.com (currently access-controlled) rather than a public API program.

providers.name: Silo Finance
providers.description: Silo Finance is a decentralized, non-custodial lending protocol built around isolated money markets. Each market pairs a single collateral asset with a borrowable asset in its own risk silo, so the failure or manipulation of one asset cannot cascade into unrelated markets — the isolation model that distinguishes Silo from pooled lenders. The protocol is delivered as onchain smart contracts (Silo V1, V2 and V3) deployed across Ethereum and other EVM chains, with an application at silo.finance, developer and protocol-architecture documentation at docs.silo.finance, third-party security audits, and an open GitHub organization publishing the contracts, subgraph and indexer. Silo Finance is backed by Electric Capital and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a DeFi lending provider.

providers.name: EZKL
providers.description: EZKL (by Zkonduit Inc.) is a developer-friendly engine for verifiable AI and analytics that generates zero-knowledge proofs (ZK-SNARKs, Halo2) for machine learning model inference. Given a model in ONNX format and sample input, EZKL automatically compiles a proving circuit and produces a cryptographic proof that a computation ran correctly without revealing the underlying private data or model weights. Proofs are verifiable on-chain (EVM-compatible), in the browser, or on edge devices. EZKL ships as a command-line tool, Python and JavaScript (WebAssembly) bindings, and a Rust library, and supports tree-based models, transformers, CNNs, and RNNs. Lilith is its high-performance compute cluster for cloud-scale proof generation. The codebase was audited by Trail of Bits and is developed in the open at github.com/zkonduit/ezkl.

providers.name: Blackbird Labs
providers.description: Blackbird Labs is a New York-based hospitality technology company building a payments and loyalty platform for restaurants and their guests. Its flagship product, Blackbird Pay, is a blockchain-powered payment network that charges restaurants roughly 2% per transaction and settles automatically at the table, while diners earn $FLY loyalty rewards by checking in and can redeem points across participating restaurants. Payments run over Flynet, a layer-three transaction protocol built on Coinbase's Base, and membership is represented by an NFC-tapped NFT. Founded by Resy and Eater co-founder Ben Leventhal, Blackbird is backed by Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Coinbase Ventures, and Amex Ventures. Blackbird operates as a consumer mobile app and a merchant platform and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Earn.com
providers.description: Earn.com was a cryptocurrency startup founded in 2013 as 21e6 and later known as 21 Inc and 21.co, backed by a16z and others, which raised over $116 million. It began as a Bitcoin mining venture selling the 21 Bitcoin Computer, then pivoted to a paid-messaging marketplace where senders paid recipients in cryptocurrency to read and reply to email. Coinbase acquired Earn.com in April 2018 for a reported $120 million, and co-founder Balaji Srinivasan became Coinbase's first Chief Technology Officer. The standalone Earn.com product was retired and the brand was folded into Coinbase Earn, the learn-and-earn program. As of July 2026 the earn.com domain issues a blanket HTTP 301 redirect for every path to https://www.coinbase.com/earn, and no developer, documentation, or API subdomain resolves. Earn.com therefore has no independent API surface; any remaining API capability lives under Coinbase.

providers.name: LedgiFi
providers.description: LedgiFi (formerly Krypto Ledgers) is a Latin American cryptocurrency tax and portfolio-tracking platform founded in 2020 and headquartered in Antofagasta, Chile. The product syncs a user's transaction history from exchanges and wallets — Binance, Coinbase, Kraken and MetaMask among them — normalizes it across more than 25,000 assets, and computes realized capital gains using the valuation methods and monetary-correction adjustments each jurisdiction requires, so investors can file a compliant return. Its Chilean profile applies the SII's specific rules (IPC indexation and dollar-variation adjustments, Impuesto de Primera Categoría and Impuesto Global Complementario), and the platform has since expanded to Mexico, Spain, Colombia and Argentina. Alongside tax reporting it offers a portfolio view spanning crypto, stocks and ETFs, with per-asset performance and allocation. LedgiFi is a 500 Global (500 LatAm B18) portfolio company. It runs a monitored production API at api.ledgifi.com that backs its own web and mobile apps, but publishes no developer portal, no API specification and no self-service API program.

providers.name: Amp
providers.description: Amp is an Ethereum-based digital collateral token (an ERC-20 fungible token extended with ERC-1400-style partitions and ERC-777-style operator semantics) designed to collateralize and instantly settle value transfer worldwide, most notably as the collateral layer behind Flexa payments. The AMP contract (0xff20817765cb7f73d4bde2e66e067e58d11095c2) supports partitioned staking, registered collateral managers, and operator authorization, and has been independently audited by ConsenSys Diligence (June 2020) and Trail of Bits (August 2020). Amp is smart-contract-only and exposes no REST/HTTP API; its published "API reference" documents the on-chain contract interface. The project is stewarded by the Acronym Foundation and was backed by Pantera Capital.

providers.name: imgauth — API di attestazione opere digitali
providers.description: Digital-work attestation and proof-of-existence service by Spazio Genesi ETS. Clients compute a SHA-256 fingerprint locally (file bytes never leave the device) and receive a signed PDF certificate, an RFC 3161 timestamp, and an OpenTimestamps/Bitcoin anchor. Exposes a public REST API (OpenAPI 3.0.3) and a hosted remote MCP server for agents.

providers.name: Meanwhile
providers.description: Meanwhile is the first BMA-licensed innovative life insurer in Bermuda, offering whole life insurance policies denominated entirely in Bitcoin rather than fiat. Its BTC Life product lets customers pay premiums in Bitcoin that grow at a guaranteed rate in Bitcoin terms, borrow tax-free against up to 90% of policy value after one year, and pass a full day-one death benefit to beneficiaries without managing wallets or seed phrases. The company is backed by Pantera, Bain Capital Crypto, Sam Altman, Northwestern Mutual, and Framework Ventures, and raised $82M in October 2025. Meanwhile publishes no public developer API, portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Rugspull Read API
providers.description: A read-only, GET-only discovery-cache REST API for Rugspull, a self-described high-risk parody DeFi protocol on BNB Smart Chain (chain id 56). Exposes rebuildable discovery/indexed-event data with no write, settlement, or transaction-proxy operations; on-chain BSC contracts remain the source of financial truth. Unauthenticated, free, best-effort, with no published rate limits or SLA.

providers.name: Arq
providers.description: Arq (formerly DolarApp) is a Latin American cross-border fintech app that gives travelers, investors, and professionals digital dollar and digital euro accounts at real market rates without hidden fees. Founded in 2021, the mobile-first platform offers currency conversion, a borderless payment card, global accounts to send and receive international payments, bill payment, PIX transfers, stock and ETF investing, and high-yield Trade and Save accounts, plus ARQ Premium and Prestige tiers. Arq raised $70M from Sequoia Capital and Founders Fund and serves over 2 million users across the Americas. Arq is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public API or developer portal; this profile captures its verified public identity and web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bright Moments DAO
providers.description: Bright Moments is an onchain art organization and decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) that produces live, in-person (IRL) generative NFT minting experiences in cities around the world. Its flagship CryptoCitizens collection (10,000 Art Blocks-powered generative portraits by artist Qian Qian) was minted 1,000 at a time across ten cities including Venice CA (CryptoVenetians), New York, Berlin, London, Mexico City, Tokyo, Buenos Aires, Paris, Venice Italy, and the Metaverse. Holding a CryptoCitizen confers membership and governance rights in the Bright Moments DAO, which was founded on-chain in March 2021. Bright Moments also runs artist collaborations/residencies, a Golden Token minting mechanism, and display software for at-home viewing. It is not a traditional API provider: the public technical surface is Ethereum/Base smart contracts, a documentation site, a DAO portal app, and a public GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Candy Fanatics (fka Candy Digital)
providers.description: Candy Digital (branded simply as "Candy") is a digital collectibles platform operating at candy.io under the tagline "Crave. Collect. Connect." It is best known for officially licensed Major League Baseball (MLB) digital trading cards and NFT drops, sold through a consumer-facing, wallet-native web application for buying, collecting, and trading licensed digital collectibles. Founded in 2021 and backed by investors including Insight Partners, the company runs an active consumer product (e.g. the 2026 MLB Base Series drops). The former candy.com domain has since been divested and is now listed for acquisition via Hilco Digital Assets; the live brand and product run at candy.io. Candy Digital is a consumer-facing product and does not currently publish a public API program, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI — this profile captures its real public web surface.

providers.name: Goin
providers.description: Goin is a European consumer fintech platform, backed by Anthemis and based in Barcelona, Spain, that helps more than 700,000 users across Europe grow their money and spend less. The app bundles automated savings (fixed daily, weekly or monthly rules and goal-based portfolios), investing, buying and selling of cryptocurrencies, cashback and rewards at hundreds of online and physical stores, gift cards and coupons, and a browser extension that surfaces discounts while shopping. Bank accounts are connected securely under Europe's PSD2 open banking regulation, and a referral program rewards users for inviting friends. Goin is a business-to-consumer mobile product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish a public developer program, API, or documentation surface. This API Evangelist profile tracks Goin as a portfolio lead and captures its public web, help, and legal presence.

providers.name: Thruster
providers.description: Thruster was a yield-first decentralized exchange (DEX) built natively on the Blast Ethereum Layer 2, offering Uniswap-style v2 and v3 concentrated liquidity AMMs, a stableswap AMM, and a token launchpad. Backed by Pantera Capital, the protocol shut down on July 29, 2025 after completing THRUST holder redemptions; its thruster.finance website is offline, while the GitBook documentation and the ThrusterX GitHub organization (Solidity contracts and audit reports) remain the surviving public record. No REST/HTTP API was published; the developer surface was on-chain smart contracts on Blast.

providers.name: Hourglass
providers.description: Hourglass is a DeFi protocol and time-bound token (TBT) infrastructure that invented a primitive for tokenizing staked, locked, or time-committed on-chain assets, letting holders trade their place in a lock-up queue for early liquidity. Its products include an RFQ marketplace built on OpenSea's Seaport for trading time-bound tokens, non-custodial on-chain vaults (including the Pre-iUSDT stable vault and the sunset Hourglass Boost product), and institutional-grade yield infrastructure that bridges on-chain DeFi capital with traditional capital markets. TBTs are semi-fungible ERC-1155 tokens issued by Hourglass custodian smart contracts on Ethereum. Launch partners included Lido, Frax, and Convex. Founded in 2022 and backed by a $4.2M seed round led by Electric Capital, with Coinbase Ventures, Circle Ventures, and others participating.

providers.name: Layer3
providers.description: Layer3 is a consumer crypto platform that bills itself as a gateway to the onchain economy, combining a gasless smart wallet with curated protocol "Activations" where users complete onchain tasks to earn CUBE rewards and the L3 token. It spans 40+ chains and 500+ applications, adds trading, staking, competitions, perks, and social features, and offers a Builder product that lets protocols launch incentivized activations, set up a Space, and distribute token rewards. It is backed by Electric Capital. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface was found during enrichment; the docs at docs.layer3.xyz cover the end-user Platform and no-code Builder products only.

providers.name: Vosbor
providers.description: Vosbor is a digital trading platform for bulk agricultural commodities, headquartered in Amsterdam with offices in Singapore and Shanghai. Founded in 2019 and backed by Lux Capital, its exchange lets trading firms and end users trade corn, wheat, soybean, palm oil and other grains and oilseeds in spot and forward markets, with integrated KYC, encrypted trade data, straight-through processing, and a WhatsApp AI broker that negotiates with multiple counterparties simultaneously. Market data is downloadable in CSV, and the company advertises data access through an API for customers, but publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Stockbit
providers.description: Stockbit (PT Stockbit Sekuritas Digital) is an Indonesian retail-investing platform and social community for the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX), letting members discuss, analyze, and trade stocks with real-time market data, fundamentals, trading ideas, news, and sentiment. The product is delivered as consumer iOS and Android apps plus a web experience, with a separate crypto brand (Stockbit Crypto). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Stockbit publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDK, or .well-known discovery surface — the profile is maintained as a consumer-app company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: T2P
providers.description: T2P Co., Ltd. (DeepPocket) is a Bangkok, Thailand fintech founded in 2011 that provides comprehensive payment solutions for enterprises of all sizes. Its products include a payment gateway (cards, mobile wallets, in-store), a white-label digital wallet platform, corporate and prepaid card issuance, spend management with real-time controls, business escrow, the DeepBlok loyalty program, and the DeepPocket consumer e-wallet app for top-ups, payments, and global money transfers. T2P is backed by 500 Global, Benchachinda Holding, DTAC Accelerate, and J Ventures, and reports serving 10M+ customers and 30+ corporate clients. T2P holds PCI DSS compliance but publishes no public developer API surface; integrations are arranged directly with the company.

providers.name: BitAccess
providers.description: Bitaccess is a Canadian blockchain company (Ottawa, founded 2013, Y Combinator) that builds the enterprise software and hardware powering Bitcoin ATM (BTM) operations and fintech businesses in more than 15 countries. Its stack includes the Bitaccess BTM operating software, the Cash API for cash-in and cash-out crypto transaction flows, and the Catena blockchain suite for publishing complex datasets to public or private blockchains via smart contracts. Bitaccess maintains an in-house HD/multisig enterprise wallet built for high-velocity applications and publishes first-party open-source client libraries under the npm @bitaccess scope and the github.com/bitaccess organization, led by the coinlib unified Node.js/TypeScript crypto-payments library. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Datavant
providers.description: Datavant is a United States health-data logistics company, formed from the 2021 merger of Datavant and Ciox Health, that connects and de-identifies healthcare data across a "network of networks" spanning 350+ real-world data partners, 80,000+ hospitals and clinics, and a majority of the largest US health systems. Its core capabilities are privacy-preserving record linkage using Datavant tokens, HIPAA Expert Determination and de-identification, medical record retrieval / release of information, and real-world evidence generation for life sciences, payers, providers, and government. Datavant's integration surface is enterprise and partner/contract gated - an access-controlled API host exists at api.datavant.com (returns HTTP 403 to anonymous callers) but Datavant does not publish a self-serve public developer portal, a downloadable OpenAPI specification, or a FHIR CapabilityStatement. Home market is the United States.

providers.name: Lootex
providers.description: Lootex is a Web3 infrastructure and AI application development company with eight years in the blockchain space, backed by 500 Global. It built a multi-chain NFT marketplace (Seaport protocol with aggregator support), the Lootex Studio minting tool, the Biru social platform, and Lootex Plus (an API and SDK offering to mint, trade, and integrate NFTs into apps and games). Its core marketplace infrastructure — a NestJS backend and Next.js frontend with blockchain event indexing and Web3 wallet authentication — is published as open source under Apache-2.0. Lootex is now sunsetting its consumer products (marketplace, Studio, and Biru wind down on 2026-04-04; assets stay in users' own non-custodial wallets) and pivoting to full-stack AI/Web3 development partnerships and open-source contributions.

providers.name: Autograph
providers.description: Autograph is a fan engagement and digital collectibles platform co-founded by Tom Brady and operated by LFG NFTs Corp. It recognizes and rewards fans by turning their passion for athletes, artists, and celebrities into access, experiences, and exclusive rewards. The platform consolidates fan communities and content into a single app, using web3 and NFT technology to let creators and public figures collaborate directly with their supporters. Autograph is a consumer product with no public developer API program at this time; api.autograph.io serves the app backend and docs.autograph.io is a private GitBook.

providers.name: Ejara
providers.description: Ejara is a Cameroon-based, regulated fintech platform giving people across Francophone Africa and its diaspora access to digital savings and investment products through a mobile app. Founded in 2020 in Douala by Nelly Chatue-Diop, Baptiste Andrieux, and Tierno Tall, Ejara lets users save from as little as 1,000 CFA francs in BEAC-guaranteed savings plans earning up to 5% annual interest, and buy, sell, and self-custody cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stablecoins using blockchain-based non-custodial wallets. The company is licensed by COSUMAF in the CEMAC zone (SGP-06/2021) and registered with France's Autorite des marches financiers (AMF-E2022-056), and raised an $8M Series A led by Anthemis and Dragonfly. Ejara operates as a consumer mobile application on iOS and Android rather than a public API provider; this profile tracks its developer surface, including open-source blockchain libraries on GitHub, for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Delphia
providers.description: Delphia (Delphia Technologies Inc., Toronto, Canada) is an AI-driven quantitative investment firm that puts alternative data to work in systematic trading strategies. Originally a consumer robo-advisor and data-reward token platform backed by a $60M Series A led by Multicoin Capital, Delphia pivoted in 2024 to institutional quant investing with its Oracle Alpha hedge fund and Tilt trend platform. As of this writing Delphia publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company identity plus its live security and well-known surfaces.

providers.name: Plural Finance
providers.description: Plural Finance is a financial operating system for infrastructure — a programmable execution layer that automates ownership, payments, compliance, and reporting across the lifecycle of infrastructure and energy assets. Its AssetOS platform tokenizes infrastructure assets such as distributed renewables, data centers, public-private partnerships, and electricity sales contracts, so institutional and individual investors can underwrite, monitor, and trade projects, with smart-contract execution of capital contributions and distributions and embedded regulatory controls. The company holds broker-dealer licensing and is backed by Paradigm. Plural currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is through its institutional web application.

providers.name: Nova Labs
providers.description: Nova Labs, Inc. is the company behind the Helium Network, a decentralized wireless network that replaces traditional carrier infrastructure with community-hosted Hotspots and is coordinated on the Solana blockchain and incentivized with the HNT token. Helium operates two networks: a global LoRaWAN network for low-power IoT devices and a cellular/Wi-Fi offload network for mobile connectivity (Helium Mobile). Nova Labs open-sources the network's protocol surface as gRPC/Protobuf service definitions (the helium/proto config, router, and proof-of-coverage services) and publishes a set of first-party client libraries, a command-line tool, and Rust crates for cryptography and protobuf types. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from Nova Labs' public developer surface; much of the legacy Helium IoT REST API tooling is archived following the network's migration to Solana.

providers.name: Abra
providers.description: Abra is a digital asset wealth and treasury management platform founded in 2014 that provides institutional-grade services for high-net-worth individuals, institutions, corporations, and family offices across all 50 US states. Its products include Vault (segregated-account custody built on Fireblocks MPC wallet technology), proprietary Yield strategies on BTC, ETH, SOL and stablecoins, crypto-backed loans up to 50% LTV, and institutional treasury management, OTC execution, staking, and advisory. The company reports $10B+ in transaction volume and $2.5B+ in loans processed, and is backed by Pantera Capital. Abra does not currently publish a public developer API, API documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its public identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: Bloxtel, Inc.
providers.description: Bloxtel, Inc. builds a decentralized private 5G platform that lets enterprises deploy standalone 5G networks in hours. Its all-in-one 5G Access Point runs Open6GC, Bloxtel's decentralized network core, and pairs with tokenized dSIM electronic-SIM technology and a Web3 Operator dApp for configuring networks, managing dSIM subscriptions, and AI-powered predictive maintenance. Solutions span indoor coverage, SIM-swap protection, neutral hosting, peer nodes, and network analytics, targeting lower latency, reduced threat surface, and lower cost versus traditional carrier deployments. Backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Bloxtel publishes a marketing and lead-generation site only, with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK yet available.

providers.name: Bridg Payment Solutions
providers.description: Bridg Payment Solutions Ltd. is a Dubai-based fintech founded in 2013 by Moussa Beidas and Nadim Jarudi. Its patent-pending OneConnect technology turns any smartphone into a point-of-sale terminal and mobile wallet, using Bluetooth to let two phones exchange card payments even when only one (or neither) has an internet connection by treating the devices as a network of offline ledgers. Bridg targets delivery drivers, in-flight retail on low-cost carriers, and merchants who need to accept debit and credit card payments without dedicated hardware, and offers the product white-labeled to merchants and payment partners. The company advertises PCI DSS and Visa compliance and is backed by 500 Global, TURN8, MetLife Foundation, Village Capital, and the European Commission. This profile was enriched from the public marketing site; Bridg publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Freeport Markets
providers.description: Freeport Markets is a Y Combinator-backed fintech and crypto trading platform offering 24/7 self-custody access to stocks, crypto, commodities, forex, rates, perpetual futures and pre-IPO shares, with leverage and AI analysts that turn social and financial media into a real-time feed of market-moving news and actionable trade ideas. The consumer product is delivered primarily through iOS and Android apps and emphasizes self-custody, "smart money" signal tracking (insiders, politicians, hedge funds and social media), and unified DeFi opportunities in a single interface. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Freeport Markets does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Halogen Capital
providers.description: Halogen Capital is Malaysia's first and only licensed digital asset fund manager, regulated by the Securities Commission Malaysia (License eCMSL/A0388/2023) and headquartered in Kuala Lumpur. The firm gives high-net-worth individuals, family offices, corporates, and institutional investors regulated access to cryptocurrency and traditional assets through unit trust structures, offering Shariah-compliant Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Crypto Titans basket funds alongside a MYR liquid fund, a ringgit income fund, and an enhanced income fund, all secured with multi-signature custody. Backed by Kenanga Investment Bank and 500 Global, Halogen manages roughly RM400 million in assets under management and is expanding into real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web presence and domain-security posture; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: MonkeyTilt
providers.description: MonkeyTilt is a crypto-native online casino and sportsbook where players deposit, wager, and cash out in cryptocurrency across slots, table games, live dealer, and sports betting. The platform rewards play with points, prize drops, and the Tilt Club VIP program (bonuses and merch drops), and is backed by Pantera Capital. MonkeyTilt is a consumer gaming product: it runs an internal application API (disallowed to crawlers in robots.txt) but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Regular Finance
providers.description: Regular Finance (Regular) is a French fintech offering a consumer digital-asset yield account. Customers deposit euros by bank transfer and earn roughly 5.50% annual interest paid daily, backed by regulated stablecoins such as EURC and USDC placed into on-chain liquidity pools and yield protocols. Withdrawals are free at any time and no crypto knowledge is required. Regular is a Techstars-backed company headquartered in France; the product is entirely consumer-facing (web and mobile app at app.regular.eu) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Fold
providers.description: Fold (NASDAQ: FLD) is a bitcoin financial services company founded in 2014 and based in Atlanta, Georgia, billed as the first publicly traded bitcoin financial services company. Fold makes it easy for individuals and businesses to earn, save, and use bitcoin through consumer products including the Fold App, the Fold Bitcoin Rewards Credit Card, the Fold Debit Card, and the Fold Bitcoin Gift Card marketplace, paying real bitcoin rewards (not points or a proprietary token) on everyday purchases and bill payments. Bitcoin custody and Lightning Network payouts are powered by partners such as BitGo and OpenNode. Fold is a consumer-facing fintech application and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Stader Labs
providers.description: Stader Labs is a non-custodial, smart-contract-driven liquid staking platform for Proof-of-Stake networks. It lets retail users, exchanges, and custodians stake crypto and receive tokenized liquid staking tokens (ETHx, MaticX, BNBx, NEARx and others) that stay usable across 40+ DeFi protocols while earning auto-compounding rewards, with no lock-up and no minimum stake. Stader operates as multi-chain middleware infrastructure across Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Hedera, Fantom, and NEAR, and its contracts have been audited by Sigma Prime, Halborn, Peckshield, Code4rena, and OtterSec. The project is on-chain and open source rather than a REST/OpenAPI provider; developer surface area is Solidity/Go/Rust smart contracts, node software, and CLI tooling on GitHub.

providers.name: Xalts
providers.description: Xalts (operated by Tokuten Pte Ltd) is an Accel-backed fintech building an AI agent platform for corporate treasury and finance teams — a copilot that automates trade finance operations (guarantees, trade payments, documentary credit and collections), liquidity management, and revenue operations. Task-specific agents learn internal processes and policies and integrate with ERPs, accounting systems, payment processors, and banks through the company's Omni Connect Protocol, which provides multi-bank connectivity via a single API. Xalts does not currently publish a public developer portal or API documentation; its connectivity APIs are offered to enterprise customers.

providers.name: Mukuru
providers.description: Mukuru is a Cape Town-headquartered, pan-African fintech and one of the continent's largest formal remittance providers, serving over 16 million customers across Southern, Eastern and Western Africa, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. Founded in 2004 to make sending money home faster and more affordable for the African diaspora, Mukuru now operates a broader financial services platform spanning international and domestic money transfers, the Mukuru Card (a prepaid card product), Mukuru Wallet (a mobile money wallet available in markets such as Botswana for airtime, electricity, and bill payments), Mukuru Pay (cash-based online checkout at retail partners), and Mukuru Funeral Cover (life insurance with cross-border repatriation benefits underwritten by Guardrisk Life). The company is licensed as a South African Financial Services Provider (FSP 45517) and registered Credit Provider (NCRCP9244), and reaches customers through a hybrid network of branches, retail booths, USSD, WhatsApp, web, and native Android, iOS, and Huawei AppGallery apps, supported by more than 320,000 pay-in and pay-out locations. An enterprise arm — branded under the Mukuru Enterprise / MukuruPay umbrella — offers collections and disbursements rails to businesses sending funds into or paying out across Africa. Mukuru does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source client; its Mukuru GitHub organization contains only archived forks of upstream infrastructure tooling (Drone, Helm, Puppet, PHP Docker images) and no Mukuru-authored libraries. Integrations with the Mukuru Enterprise platform are arranged through direct commercial engagement rather than a self-service developer program.

providers.name: Sovryn
providers.description: Sovryn is a Bitcoin-native, non-custodial decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol built on Rootstock (RSK). It offers spot and margin trading, perpetual swaps, 0% interest Bitcoin-backed loans (Zero), the Sovryn Dollar (DLLR) Bitcoin-backed stablecoin, yield and liquidity pools, and SOV governance staking, operating as a DAO. Sovryn also incubated BitcoinOS, a zk-powered rollup and multi-VM execution stack for Bitcoin. Developers integrate through open-source smart contracts, a GraphQL subgraph, an indexer HTTP data API, and first-party JavaScript SDKs published under the @sovryn and @sovryn-zero npm scopes.

providers.name: Geode
providers.description: Geode Finance is a decentralized, trustless staking infrastructure protocol on Ethereum (with an earlier Avalanche v1 deployment) that lets anyone create and operate permissionless, configurable liquid-staking pools without intermediaries. Through its Portal router, isolated storage, dual governance, staking derivatives (gETH / gAVAX), an operator marketplace, withdrawal contracts, bound liquidity pools, and the Telescope oracle system, entities can launch their own liquid staking derivatives, isolate risk profiles, run KYC/AML-segregated pools, and earn sustainable maintenance-fee revenue. Developers integrate via the geodefi Python SDK and geo-vue UI components.

providers.name: Blackbird Labs Inc
providers.description: Blackbird Labs is the company behind Blackbird, a payments-and-loyalty app for the restaurant industry. Diners earn status, perks, points, and the $FLY rewards token by checking in and paying at partner restaurants, while restaurants gain a direct guest relationship and improved economics. Settlement runs on Flynet, a layer-three protocol built on Coinbase's Base blockchain. Founded by Resy and Eater co-founder Ben Leventhal, Blackbird is live across cities including New York, San Francisco, Charleston, Denver, and New Orleans, and raised $50 million in 2025. Backed by investors including QED Investors and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z crypto). Blackbird is a consumer application and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI description, or developer portal; this profile captures its public company and security posture surface.

providers.name: Planetary
providers.description: Planetary is a decentralized, peer-to-peer social networking company built on the Secure Scuttlebutt (SSB) protocol, offering an iOS app for algorithm-free social media where users own and store their data locally with no advertising and no data selling. The team has since migrated its design, app, and philosophy to the Nostr protocol under a new app, nos.social. The project is fully open source, developed in the open on GitHub, and is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Planetary exposes no commercial REST/HTTP API; its developer surface is the underlying SSB/Nostr protocol documentation (RPC methods, replication, blobs) rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Warbler Labs Incorporated
providers.description: Warbler Labs is the San Francisco-based software company founded in 2020 by former Coinbase engineers Blake West and Mike Sall that builds and maintains Goldfinch, a decentralized credit protocol on Ethereum for stablecoin lending to real-world borrowers without crypto collateral, and UID (Unique Identity), a KYC/KYB-compliant on-chain identity credential. Warbler Labs is the core development team behind the Goldfinch protocol, its smart contracts, oracles, and subgraph data layer, and publishes developer documentation for building on and integrating with the protocol. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Coinbase Ventures, IDEO CoLab, Kindred Ventures, and others, and was surfaced through the a16z portfolio. Its developer surface is primarily on-chain (Solidity smart contracts, The Graph subgraph for querying protocol data, and the UID credential) rather than a hosted REST API.

providers.name: Finoa
providers.description: Finoa is a Berlin-based, BaFin-regulated digital asset infrastructure provider serving institutional investors, asset managers, family offices, venture capital funds, and regulated crypto service providers. Its platform combines qualified custody, in-custody staking, and prime brokerage across 170+ digital assets and 12 Layer-1 networks, with security and governance controls built for institutional and regulatory requirements. Finoa exposes a gated institutional API surface (api.finoa.io) and a client platform (login.finoa.io / app.finoa.io) rather than a public self-serve developer program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Skip
providers.description: Skip (originally Skip Protocol, skip.money) is the interchain infrastructure company that rebranded to Cosmos Labs and is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Interchain Foundation, leading engineering and growth for the Cosmos blockchain stack. Its skip.money and skip.build domains now redirect to cosmos.network. The team maintains the open-source Cosmos SDK, the Inter-Blockchain Communication protocol (IBC), the CometBFT consensus engine, and Cosmos EVM — the most widely adopted Layer 1 blockchain toolkit, deployed across 200+ chains. There is no independent Skip-branded hosted API; the public developer surface is the Cosmos SDK node REST + gRPC interfaces documented at docs.cosmos.network, with source on the cosmos GitHub organization.

providers.name: Web3 Foundation
providers.description: Web3 Foundation is a Swiss nonprofit founded in 2017 by Gavin Wood that funds research and development teams building the foundation of a decentralized web (Web3). It stewards and supports the Polkadot and Kusama networks, operates a research hub and an education/wiki program, and historically ran the Web3 Foundation Grants Program (now discontinued) to seed open-source software and protocol research. It is a funding and research organization rather than a traditional API provider: it publishes no public REST/OpenAPI surface, but does maintain an RFC 9116 security.txt and a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure program.

providers.name: Bitculator
providers.description: Modern cryptocurrency REST API providing programmatic read access to crypto market data including coins, prices, markets, exchanges, wallets, global market data, sentiment, indicators, liquidations, conversions, calculators, editorial content, alarms, and webhooks. Version 1.0.0 with 70+ endpoints across 15 groups.

providers.name: Cogni
providers.description: Cogni is a non-custodial cryptocurrency wallet and digital-asset management app that consolidates cash, crypto, and NFTs in a single mobile experience. Users hold their own private keys, back up their seed phrase to iCloud, manage assets across multiple blockchains and Layer 2 networks, store and view NFTs, and connect to web3 dApps directly from the app. Backed by Techstars, Cogni is a consumer-facing mobile product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time; this profile captures its public web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Konga
providers.description: Konga is a Lagos, Nigeria-based e-commerce company founded in July 2012 and now operating as Nigeria's leading online shopping marketplace, combining a first-party retail business with a third-party seller marketplace across consumer electronics, mobile phones, home appliances, fashion, groceries, beauty, and lifestyle categories. Konga runs a vertically integrated stack alongside its storefront: KongaPay, a Central Bank of Nigeria-licensed and NDIC-insured payments platform offering checkout, transfers, virtual accounts, multi-currency wallets, POS, bill payments, savings, and merchant payouts; Konga Travel & Tours, an IATA-certified travel agency providing flight bookings, hotels, and vacation packages; Konga Health (Medical Direct); Konga Foods/Groceries; KongaNow same-day delivery; and KXpress Logistics for nationwide fulfillment. Konga's revenue model spans marketplace commissions, first-party retail margin, KongaPay transaction fees, logistics fees, travel agency commissions, and seller advertising. Konga does not operate a unified public developer program: the marketplace exposes no documented public REST API for orders, products, or sellers; KongaPay published Android, iOS, and WooCommerce SDKs and SDK docs at kongapay.github.io, but that GitHub organization was archived on July 1, 2023, and the current KPay aggregator API documentation lives at kpayment-org.gitbook.io with limited public surface area focused on POS, Web Payment Gateway, Virtual Account, and Payment Link integrations for approved merchants. As a result, Konga is profiled here as a provider index rather than as an actively documented public-API company.

providers.name: MyStars FaaS — Fulfilment API
providers.description: A B2B Fragment-as-a-Service (FaaS) fulfilment REST API for programmatically buying and reselling Telegram Stars and Telegram Premium, delivered to any Telegram @username, paid on-chain in TON (GRAM) or USDT (TON). Non-custodial, no KYC. Offers versioned /v1 endpoints for pricing, recipient checks, product catalog, and order lifecycle, with signed webhooks and official TypeScript and Python SDKs.

providers.name: Ballet
providers.description: Ballet is a consumer cryptocurrency cold-storage company founded by Bobby Lee that makes physical, non-electronic wallet cards based on the BIP38 open-source standard, letting people store Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and 1,000+ coins and NFTs safe from electronic hacking and preventable user error. The physical REAL Series card holds the keys; a companion mobile app, Ballet Crypto, lets holders check balances and market value and add assets. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Ballet is a hardware/consumer product rather than a developer platform, so it publishes no public API — this profile captures its identity, security posture, and open-source footprint.

providers.name: Grapes
providers.description: Grape (Grape Protocol / GrapeDAO, built by Grape-Labs) is Solana-based decentralized infrastructure that gives online communities and DAOs a set of mainnet-ready primitives for identity, reputation, verification, access control, rewards, and governance. Its products include OG (Vine) Reputation Spaces for season-based on-chain reputation, Grape Verification for identity attestation, the Grape Access Protocol (GPASS) for token/credential-gated access, a GSPL DAO directory, a multi-chain Grape Wallet, and a suite of Discord automation bots. Grape ships no REST/OpenAPI surface; developers integrate through first-party TypeScript SDKs (npm) that wrap its Solana programs directly. Backed by Multicoin Capital, it was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: HODL Media
providers.description: HODL Media (hodl.mobi) is the maker of HODL Real-Time Cryptocurrency, a consumer mobile application for iOS and Android that tracks cryptocurrency and stock market prices in real time. The app aggregates pricing from 180+ global exchanges, offers customizable charting with technical indicators, price alerts and bracket management, portfolio tracking with exchange and wallet synchronization (Coinbase Pro, Binance, Ethereum wallets), aggregated news and social feeds, and stock market data from NYSE and NASDAQ. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile HODL Media publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic documentation; this repo is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead.

providers.name: Improbable
providers.description: Improbable (Improbable Worlds Ltd) is a London-based technology company and venture builder. Founded in 2012, it originally built SpatialOS, a distributed simulation and networking platform for large-scale real-time multiplayer games, and later Morpheus / M² (MSquared), a network of interoperable metaverse worlds. Today Improbable operates primarily as a venture builder and capital allocator, partnering with founders to launch and scale companies across AI, Web3 and the metaverse. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its historical developer surface centered on the SpatialOS Platform SDK, Worker SDK and the `spatial` CLI (distributed via NuGet), plus the improbable-eng and spatialos GitHub organizations; the standalone documentation, status and IMS subdomains have since been retired as the company pivoted away from a standalone developer platform.

providers.name: Adanos Market Sentiment API
providers.description: Key-authenticated REST/JSON API for financial market sentiment analytics across Reddit, X.com, news, and Polymarket, plus stock news and crypto sentiment. Provides Buzz Score, Trend Detection, and directional Sentiment signals for traders, fintech, quant/research teams, and AI agents.

providers.name: Aella Credit
providers.description: Aella (Aella Credit) is a technology-driven microfinance bank licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), building consumer and business financial infrastructure across Africa. Its consumer app offers savings, low-interest and same-day loans, bill payments, and high-yield savings accounts, while its Fintech-as-a-Service platform exposes that infrastructure to businesses through a developer-facing API gateway. Published API capabilities include wallet-as-a- service (create and manage digital wallets with real-time balances and full ledger support), KYC/identity verification via BVN and NIN, bank-account lookup and validation, sub-accounts and pooled fund structures for platforms and marketplaces, and direct-debit recurring collections. A live Aella Merchant API is hosted at api.aellaapp.com and a merchant dashboard at merchant.aellaapp.com, though the provider does not yet publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile was seeded as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: BTC War Live Market Data API
providers.description: Public, read-only real-time crypto market-data API from btcwar.net, exposing live Binance Spot order-flow snapshots and single-market observations for nine USDT pairs as JSON and Schema.org JSON-LD. Ships a complete agent-native discovery stack: OpenAPI 3.1, Arazzo workflow, hosted MCP server, and llms.txt.

providers.name: Jingle Pay
providers.description: Jingle Pay is a DFSA-regulated (Dubai Financial Services Authority) digital financial services fintech headquartered in the UAE, offering an all-in-one mobile money account for cross-border remittances, peer-to-peer payments, real-time multi-currency exchange, and Mastercard-powered card payments. Founded and led by CEO Amir Fardghassemi, the company serves the UAE, Pakistan, Bahrain, and Canada, and reports having processed over $3.5 billion across 8M+ transactions to 150 countries for 1.5M+ unique senders. It is backed by strategic partners and investors including Bank Alfalah, MoneyGram, Mastercard, and 500 Global. Jingle Pay operates as a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Stone Co
providers.description: Stone Co. (NASDAQ: STNE) is a Brazilian financial services and payment technology company headquartered in São Paulo. Stone provides card acquiring (POS), digital banking, business management software, and credit products to entrepreneurs and small-to-medium businesses across more than 5,500 Brazilian cities, and is the fourth-largest acquirer in Brazil following its acquisition of Elavon's Brazilian operations. Stone operates several developer-facing platforms: Connect Stone (a POS integration API for in-store payment automation and "infinite shelf" omnichannel inventory), Stone Open Banking (a RESTful banking API for account, balance, TED, PIX, and payment-link operations against Stone accounts and consented third-party accounts), the Stone SDK Android (for embedding card-present payments into Android apps and Pinpad/POS devices), AutoTEF (PIN-pad-based self-service TEF integration), the Conciliação Stone XML reconciliation feed, and Pagar.me (Stone's online/PSP gateway covering orders, charges, customers, subscriptions, split payments, recurring billing, tokenization, and 3DS). Authentication is OAuth2 / PEM-keyed JWT for Open Banking and API-key / credential-based for the other surfaces. Onboarding for Open Banking and Connect Stone partners is gated through Stone's partnerships team; Pagar.me and the Android SDK are self-service. Documentation is primarily in Portuguese and concentrated at docs.stone.com.br, docs.openbank.stone.com.br, connect-stone.stone.com.br, conciliacao.stone.com.br, and docs.pagar.me.

providers.name: Braavos
providers.description: Braavos is a self-custody smart-contract wallet for Bitcoin and Starknet, available as a browser extension and mobile app. Built on Starknet account abstraction, it adds hardware-backed two-factor signing (mobile secure element and passkeys), session keys for dApps, gas abstraction, in-wallet swaps, staking, and fiat on-ramp. Its developer surface is the injected Starknet wallet API (get-starknet), the Braavos Cairo account contracts, and first-party JavaScript libraries (session keys, deeplinks, StarkNet URLs, dApp metadata) published under the myBraavos GitHub organization. Braavos does not publish a hosted REST API or OpenAPI. Sector: crypto. Backed by Pantera Capital.

providers.name: OneConnect
providers.description: OneConnect Financial Technology (NYSE: OCFT; HKEX: 6638) is a technology-as-a-service platform for financial institutions, incorporated in 2015 as an associate of China's Ping An Group to externalize its banking and insurance technology. Its cloud-native, microservices platform spans digital banking, digital insurance, and the Gamma platform (AI voice, computer vision, blockchain and big-data analytics), serving hundreds of banks and insurers across China and Southeast Asia with ready-to-integrate financial technology components exposed through Open APIs. OneConnect raised a US$650M Series A in 2018 from investors including the SoftBank Vision Fund and SBI Group. Its APIs are delivered as enterprise B2B integrations rather than a public self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: PROOF
providers.description: PROOF is a digital art and NFT platform built on the belief that "art is proof of our collective humanity." It is the company behind Moonbirds (its flagship profile-picture collection), the 1,000-member PROOF Collective, and collections including Oddities, Mythics, and the Grails art-collector experience, alongside the Lunar Society community-governance program, a research arm, live events, and a podcast. PROOF is backed by a16z and Kindred Ventures. Its public surface is a consumer/collector documentation site (docs.proof.xyz) and marketing site; PROOF does not currently publish a programmatic developer API, OpenAPI spec, SDKs, or webhooks.

providers.name: Auto Finance
providers.description: Auto Finance is a decentralized finance (DeFi) liquidity-management protocol built by Tokemak. Its core product, Autopools, are automated onchain vaults that autonomously optimize, rebalance, and auto-compound liquidity-provider yield across major DeFi venues (Curve, Fluid, Inverse, Morpho, AAVE) and networks (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base), abstracting away the complexity of manual LP management. The protocol is governed and secured through AUTO token staking, and its onchain surface is a public set of audited Solidity smart contracts rather than a REST API. Documentation is published via GitBook with an agent-readable llms.txt index.

providers.name: Baton Systems
providers.description: Baton Systems is a post-trade settlement and payments technology provider founded in 2016, headquartered in Silicon Valley with offices in London, New York, and Chennai. Its CORE platform (Core-FX, Core-Payments, Core-Liquidity, and Core-Collateral) uses distributed ledger technology (DLT) and payment-versus-payment (PvP) settlement to orchestrate real-time FX settlement, intraday liquidity management, collateral optimization, and post-trade payment control for global banks and financial institutions. Baton operates a live FX PvP settlement service and processes roughly USD 30 billion daily for seven of the nine largest Western global systemically important banks, having settled trillions in aggregate value. Data flows integrate over APIs and standard financial formats including ISO 20022, SWIFT MT, FIXML, and XML.

providers.name: PsyOptions
providers.description: PsyOptions is a decentralized options protocol built on Solana by Mithraic Labs, providing on-chain American-style options contracts originally designed for use with the Serum/OpenBook DEX. Rather than a hosted REST API, it exposes its functionality through open-source on-chain Anchor/BPF programs and first-party TypeScript client libraries (the @mithraic-labs npm scope: psy-american, psyoptions, market-meta, psy-token-registry, psy-metrics) plus a Rust crate. The project has since been sunset: its documentation and marketing sites are shut down, though the GitHub repositories and published packages remain available for reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. Sector: crypto / DeFi.

providers.name: Saffron Finance
providers.description: Saffron Finance is a decentralized peer-to-peer interest-rate risk adjustment protocol built on Ethereum. Underlying DeFi yield is transformed by a smart-contract vault system according to each user's indicated risk preference, splitting deposits into senior (fixed-income, risk-averse) and junior (variable, risk-seeking) tranches across Uniswap V3 fixed-income vaults. The protocol is governed by the Saffron DAO and its SFI token, and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital in the crypto-web3 sector. Saffron is an on-chain protocol rather than a hosted web-API provider: its developer surface is Solidity smart contracts, published documentation, audits, and whitepapers rather than a REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Stablecore
providers.description: Stablecore provides digital-asset banking infrastructure that lets banks and credit unions offer stablecoins, tokenized deposits, digital-asset accounts and exchange, and digital-asset-based lending inside their existing core, digital-banking and compliance stacks. The platform targets cross-border payments, treasury management, digital-asset investing, crypto on/off-ramps and stablecoin sponsor banking, with a multi-provider design intended to avoid vendor lock-in and built-in compliance tooling. Stablecore is SOC 2 compliant and an ABA Partner Network member; investors include Coinbase Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners and Bank of Utah. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and product site plus a blog, but no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Sweatcoin
providers.description: Sweatcoin is a health-and-fitness app that converts a user's physical steps and movement into a digital currency ("sweatcoins") that can be redeemed for gadgets, subscriptions, travel vouchers, charity donations, and cryptocurrency. Its proprietary movement-validation algorithms count outdoor steps while, the company states, not selling location data. Sweatcoin reports being a top-3 health & fitness app worldwide with tens of millions of users across 180+ countries, and partners with brands and organizations (NHS, Apple, Amazon and 600+ others) through sponsored challenges, clubs, boosts and an affiliate marketplace. The team also launched the Sweat Economy ($SWEAT), a NEAR-Protocol "movement economy" token, and the Sweat Wallet app, turning tracked movement into on-chain digital value. Sweatcoin exposes no public REST/OpenAPI developer surface; integration is via partner and marketplace programs and the SWEAT on-chain token.

providers.name: Vixtra
providers.description: Vixtra (VIXTRA Tecnologia e Serviços Financeiros LTDA., CNPJ 43.443.444/0001-04) is a Brazilian trade-finance fintech founded in July 2021 and headquartered in São Paulo, positioning itself as "the Trade Banking of the Brazilian importer." It pioneers financing for importers using in-transit maritime cargo as collateral, and delivers credit, foreign exchange, guarantees, and cash-flow management for foreign trade from a single digital platform. Its products include Crédito Flex (revolving working-capital credit), Crédito Pré (pre-shipment import financing), Câmbio Fácil (100% digital commercial FX), Trade Banking (the unified operations platform), and a Vixtra stablecoin for cross-border payments. Vixtra operates as a banking correspondent of BMP Money Plus SCD and an FX correspondent of Ebury Banco de Câmbio, has raised roughly US$36M (US$30M debt + US$6M seed extension) led by QED Investors with Valor Capital Group, Endeavor Promessas, NXTP Ventures, Actyus, and BluStone, and processes data in compliance with Brazil's LGPD. No public developer portal or API is currently published; the api.vixtra.com host backs the customer application and returns 403 to anonymous callers.

providers.name: Animoca Brands
providers.description: Animoca Brands is a Web3 company focused on advancing digital property rights and building the open metaverse through blockchain technology, gaming, and digital assets. Founded in Hong Kong, the company operates a portfolio of consumer products including The Sandbox, Moca Network (digital identity), Open Campus (education), and Anichess, alongside institutional offerings such as Anchorpoint Financial (stablecoins and real-world assets) and NUVA (treasury management). Animoca Brands is also one of the most active investors in Web3, backing 600+ builders across gaming, infrastructure, real-world assets, and digital-ownership platforms. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network; Animoca operates primarily as a holding and investment company and does not publish a first-party public developer API.

providers.name: Keep Network
providers.description: Keep Network is a privacy-focused blockchain infrastructure project that merged with NuCypher in 2021 to form the Threshold Network. Its flagship product is tBTC, a decentralized, trust-minimized bridge that tokenizes Bitcoin as the TBTC ERC-20 token so it can be used across Ethereum DeFi without centralized custodians. Keep originally provided off-chain "keeps" — private data containers secured by a threshold ECDSA signing network and a random beacon — enabling confidential data to be used on public protocols. The developer surface is on-chain Solidity smart contracts plus first-party JavaScript/TypeScript client libraries published under the @keep-network npm scope; there is no hosted REST API. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched from the project's public GitHub org, npm packages, blog, and security.txt.

providers.name: Blocto
providers.description: Blocto is a Web3 smart-contract wallet built by Portto that lets everyday users interact with decentralized applications without managing seed phrases, using a chain-agnostic account-abstraction architecture. For developers, Blocto ships a client-side integration surface — the JavaScript Blocto SDK, a Blocto-flavored Flow Client Library (FCL) fork, plus Go, Swift and Rust SDKs — to connect dApps to the Blocto wallet for authentication, transaction signing and account-proof verification across Flow, Ethereum, Solana, Aptos, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Arbitrum and Optimism. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network from its public developer documentation and GitHub organization.

providers.name: Calastone
providers.description: Calastone operates the world's largest global funds network, connecting asset managers, distributors, custodians and platforms to automate and digitalize the investment funds marketplace. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in London, it provides order routing, settlements, share-class conversions, dividends, transfers, reporting, money market services and tokenized fund distribution. More than 4,500 clients across 58 countries and territories use the network, processing over £300 billion of investment value each month. API and messaging connectivity is delivered through client onboarding rather than a public self-service developer portal. Calastone is a wholly owned subsidiary of SS&C Technologies Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: SSNC).

providers.name: Irreverent Labs
providers.description: Irreverent Labs is a Bellevue, Washington startup founded in 2021 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Samsung Next, and Michael Ovitz. The company began by building MechaFightClub, a web3 gaming property, then pivoted to generative AI, developing video foundation models intended to let creators, game studios, and developers produce short-form video from natural-language prompts. Its current public product is Supermodel (supermodel.ai), an autonomous on-chain trading agent that watches top Hyperliquid wallets, scores their track records, and fuses crowd, technical, and prediction-market signals into trades. The company has publicly signaled intent to ship a developer API for its video generation models, but no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK has been released as of this profile.

providers.name: Anchor Protocol
providers.description: Anchor Protocol is a Terra-based decentralized finance (DeFi) savings protocol that offered a low-volatility yield on Terra stablecoin (UST) deposits, borrowing against bonded-asset (bAsset) collateral such as bLUNA and bETH, and cross-chain access through EthAnchor and xAnchor. Its developer surface is a set of first-party JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs (Anchor.js and Anchor Earn) plus on-chain CosmWasm smart contracts rather than a REST or OpenAPI web API. The project is part of the Terra ecosystem and is backed by Pantera Capital; its main web application deployment is currently disabled, though its developer documentation and npm SDK packages remain published.

providers.name: Betdex
providers.description: Betdex Labs is the team behind BetDEX, a decentralized sports betting exchange, and the Monaco Protocol — an open-source, permissionless liquidity and betting-exchange protocol built on the Solana blockchain. Rather than a traditional REST API, Betdex exposes an on-chain integration surface: Solana programs plus first-party TypeScript client libraries (@monaco-protocol/client and @monaco-protocol/admin-client on npm) that let developers create markets, place and match orders, and settle outcomes directly against the protocol. Developer resources are published at betdex.com/developers with source under the MonacoProtocol GitHub organization.

providers.name: dForce
providers.description: dForce is a decentralized stablecoin protocol powered by an integrated DeFi matrix spanning assets, lending, trading, and an omni-chain bridge. It positions itself as an AI-native on-chain capital markets platform, unifying its USX USD-pegged stablecoin, permissionless lending markets, yield vaults, a real-world-asset (RWA) marketplace, a DEX, the InteNet launchpad, and DF-native cross-chain bridging under DAO governance driven by the DF token. dForce ships as smart contracts across multiple EVM chains rather than a hosted REST API; its developer surface is on-chain contracts, open documentation, and the dforce-network GitHub organization. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: InfiniGods
providers.description: InfiniGods is a gaming studio building fun, free-to-play, Web3-powered mobile games centered around ancient mythologies. Its titles — Immortal Siege, King of Destiny, and InfiniMerge — share interoperable gaming assets, items, power-ups, and currencies that span the InfiniGods Universe (IGU). Players collect blockchain assets such as the Elder Gods (a 4,488-piece Gen 0 NFT collection that unlocks abilities and boosts scoring across all titles) and the InfiniPass VIP membership (early access, bonus play, exclusive NFT drops, and in-game boosts). The company is backed by Pantera Capital. InfiniGods is a consumer game studio with no public developer/API program; this profile captures its public web, legal, community, and code-org surface.

providers.name: Lolli
providers.description: Lolli is a bitcoin and cash-back rewards company founded in 2018 by CEO Alex Adelman, on a mission to make bitcoin accessible to everyone. Through a browser extension, website, and mobile app, Lolli gives shoppers a percentage of their purchase back in bitcoin or cash when they shop online and in-store at 25,000+ merchants including Adidas, Microsoft, Ulta, and Kroger. Merchants pay Lolli for driving sales, and Lolli shares that commission with users as rewards paid into their Lolli wallet. The company reports having distributed over $10 million in bitcoin rewards and onboarded thousands of people into bitcoin for the first time. Lolli is a consumer product; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of version-one-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Saber
providers.description: Saber is a decentralized automated market maker (AMM) on the Solana blockchain, optimized for trading and providing liquidity between mean-reverting assets such as stablecoins and wrapped or pegged tokens. Its StableSwap program delivers low-slippage swaps and capital-efficient liquidity pools. Saber does not expose a REST/HTTP API; developers integrate through its on-chain StableSwap program using first-party TypeScript SDKs (the @saberhq/* packages on npm) and Rust crates (crates.io) that construct and submit Solana transactions. The project also maintains open-source Solana tooling, an asset/pool registry, and on-chain governance. Saber was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Fintech
providers.description: Fin (fin.tech) is a crypto-native payments company that lets users and businesses move millions of dollars instantly — to other Fin users, directly into bank accounts, or across crypto rails. It provides business-grade payment rails that feel like a consumer payment app rather than crypto: instant global settlement in seconds, native support to deposit and withdraw to bank accounts, and send/receive of USDT, USDC, ETH, and BTC, while Fin abstracts the underlying crypto settlement behind a clean fintech interface. Backed by Sequoia, Multicoin, and Pantera Capital, Fin operates a private, auth-gated production API surface (api.fin.tech) and publishes an llms.txt for agents; it does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Pantera Capital portfolio company (sector: crypto) and enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: MathWallet
providers.description: MathWallet is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto-web3. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Cega
providers.description: Cega is a decentralized exotic derivatives protocol building on-chain structured products for investors: exotic options such as Fixed Coupon Notes (pure options and bond + options) and Dual Currency Swaps that generate yield with built-in downside protection. Cega is live on Ethereum Mainnet and Arbitrum One (EVM) and on Solana, and exposes its protocol to developers through first-party TypeScript SDKs on npm (@cega-fi) plus a GraphQL subgraph rather than a hosted REST API. Backed by Pantera Capital and surfaced into the API Evangelist network from its VC portfolio.

providers.name: Exotic Markets
providers.description: Exotic Markets is a decentralized options and structured-products protocol on the Solana blockchain, describing itself as the #1 options protocol on Solana and backed by Multicoin Capital. The platform lets users earn yield or buy call/put options through flexible structured products, including baskets of tokens, accumulators, and capital-preservation strategies with customizable payoffs and maturities. Access is on-chain via a Solana wallet (Phantom, Solflare) and the $EXO token powers staking, points, and protocol utility. Exotic Markets is a smart-contract DeFi protocol rather than a REST/HTTP API provider: there is no public OpenAPI, gateway, or hosted developer API surface; developer materials are limited to GitBook documentation, a GitHub organization, and community channels.

providers.name: Satellite
providers.description: Satellite IM builds privacy-focused, decentralized peer-to-peer communication software for crypto and web3 communities. Its core is Warp, a Rust interface-driven distributed data service providing end-to-end-encrypted chat, voice, video, and file sharing with data stored on IPFS. Uplink is a customizable decentralized chat application built on top of Warp. Satellite publishes no hosted REST or GraphQL API; the developer surface is the open-source Warp Rust crates and the first-party warp-wasm WebAssembly and TypeScript library. Satellite is backed by Multicoin Capital and its code is MIT licensed.

providers.name: Altius Labs
providers.description: Altius Labs builds customized, high-performance blockchain infrastructure for high-frequency onchain markets and trading applications. Founded by former Hudson River Trading engineers, Altius offers a VM-agnostic modular execution stack that decouples execution from consensus and storage to deliver parallel transaction processing, targeting 10,000+ TPS and sub-millisecond latency while remaining EVM-compatible through a hybrid architecture (Altius L1 for settlement plus a high-performance execution coprocessor). Applications retain gas fees, sequencing revenue, and governance rather than ceding them to a base layer. The stack integrates with existing L1, L2, and app chains and supports multiple virtual machines (EVM, MoveVM, CosmWasm, SolanaVM). Altius Labs is backed by Founders Fund, Pantera Capital, Archetype, and others, and positions itself as institutional-grade dedicated chain infrastructure deployable in weeks rather than years.

providers.name: AminoChain
providers.description: AminoChain operates a transparent, decentralized research ecosystem for patient-centric biomedical research. Its Specimen Center helps researchers discover and access legacy biospecimens through decentralized specimen discovery and collaboration, while its Donor Platform enables prospective participant registries and manages participant involvement in studies. The platform emphasizes privacy-preserving re-engagement, cryptographic tracking of biospecimens, auditable consent, and benefit-sharing models that return value to patients and donors. Backed by a16z. AminoChain currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Tibles
providers.description: Tibles is a digital collectibles company building authentic, engaging collecting experiences on the Flow blockchain. Its Tibles Clubhouse platform hosts multiple consumer iOS and web apps built around licensed intellectual properties — including FuggClub (Fugglers), Sk8tibles (Skateboarding Hall of Fame), OneShots (Valiant Comics), Tibles Fraggle Rock and Seussibles (Jim Henson / Dr. Seuss), and Aggretsuko (Sanrio) — offering interactive digital trading cards and NFT collections with barter-style trading, chat, and community events. Tibles is a Certified Flow Developer and publishes open-source Cadence smart contracts and an IPFS desktop client, but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Yield Guild Games
providers.description: Yield Guild Games (YGG) is a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) and one of the world's first and largest web3 gaming guilds, founded in 2020 by Gabby Dizon, Beryl Li, and the pseudonymous "Owl of Moistness" out of the Philippines. YGG invests in NFTs and blockchain-game assets, lends them to players, and shares the resulting yield with its community and YGG token holders. Its onchain Guild Protocol (launched on Base) equips guilds with a modular library of smart-contract tooling for treasury wallets, programmable quests, and contribution tracking, while YGG Play acts as a publisher for casual crypto games. The company was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), which led a $4.6M round in 2021. Note: this repository slug "yield-guide-games" preserves an upstream typo of the real company name, Yield Guild Games.

providers.name: Zebec Network
providers.description: Zebec Network is a blockchain infrastructure company (founded 2021, San Francisco; founder Sam Thapaliya) building real-time payroll, on-chain payments, multi-chain debit/crypto cards, and treasury management for web3 businesses and individuals. Its continuous-settlement streaming protocol began on Solana and now spans EVM chains, NEAR, and BNB via a Wormhole-based cross-chain bridge. Zebec exposes its capabilities to developers as a family of first-party TypeScript/JavaScript SDKs published on npm under the @zebec-network, @zebec-protocol, and @zebec-fintech scopes — covering payroll streaming, the vault, staking, the Silver/instant cards, the bridge, and the Solana DAO — documented at docs.zebec.io. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bitcoin
providers.description: Bitcoin is the original decentralized peer-to-peer digital currency and open-source protocol, first described in the 2008 whitepaper by Satoshi Nakamoto. It is not a company or a hosted commercial API; the reference implementation, Bitcoin Core, exposes a local JSON-RPC interface for node operators and application developers to query the blockchain, manage wallets, build and broadcast transactions, and interact with the peer-to-peer network. bitcoin.org and the developer documentation site at developer.bitcoin.org publish developer guides, an extensive RPC API command reference, worked examples, and reference material for building Bitcoin applications. This profile was seeded as a Ribbit Capital portfolio-sector lead and enriched from Bitcoin's public developer surface.

providers.name: Indian Energy Exchange
providers.description: Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) is India's largest electricity trading platform, operating a nationwide automated exchange for the physical delivery of electricity, renewable energy, and certificates. IEX runs Day-Ahead, Real-Time, Term-Ahead, Renewable Energy Certificate and Energy Saving Certificate market segments, matching buy and sell bids across a member network of distribution utilities, industrial and commercial consumers, and power generators. For members with sophisticated trading needs IEX offers a members-only trading API (currently for the iDAM and RTM segments) supporting order placement, trade-data retrieval and real-time monitoring for automated and high-frequency trading; access is provisioned to registered members rather than published as a public developer portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Parallel Finance
providers.description: Parallel Finance is a decentralized money-market protocol built on the Polkadot ecosystem, offering lending, staking, and borrowing where depositors can lend and stake simultaneously to earn combined yield and borrowers can post collateral to borrow. It runs as a Substrate/Polkadot parachain (Parallel mainnet and the Heiko canary network on Kusama). Rather than a REST API, developers integrate through a JSON-RPC node over WebSocket (wss://rpc.parallel.fi) using polkadot.js, aided by Parallel's first-party @parallel-finance TypeScript SDK packages on npm that supply the chain types, RPC definitions, and connection options. Source, chain specs, and the auction toolkit are published under the parallel-finance GitHub organization.

providers.name: Cartesi
providers.description: Cartesi is a Linux-based optimistic rollup protocol that lets developers build decentralized applications by running rich off-chain computation inside a sandboxed Linux virtual machine. The core of the stack is the Cartesi Machine, a deterministic RISC-V emulator that boots a real Linux userland so dApps can be written in any language (Rust, Go, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C++) using familiar libraries, then settle results on Ethereum and other EVM chains through Cartesi Rollups smart contracts. Cartesi Rollups 2.0 is the current major version, packaging an application-specific rollup as the combination of the Cartesi Machine, the Cartesi Rollups Node middleware (Rust + Go), and a set of Solidity rollup contracts that handle settlement, consensus, and data availability. The DAVE permissionless fraud-proof system provides Stage-2 trust minimization, while the Cartesi CLI (the successor to Sunodo) packages scaffolding, build, and local devnet workflows. Cartesi is stewarded by The Cartesi Foundation and the CTSI token governs the network.
