Cartesi is fully open source under Apache-2.0 and LGPL-3.0 licenses on github.com/cartesi; there is no proprietary SaaS product, but the Rollups Node ships several developer-facing surfaces — the Rollup HTTP API used by application backends, the Inspect HTTP API for read-only queries from frontends, a GraphQL reader for advance-state inputs / outputs / vouchers / notices / reports, and a JSON-RPC node API for operations.

providers.name: Chipper Cash
providers.description: Chipper Cash is a pan-African fintech (legal entities Critical Ideas, Inc. and Voyse Technologies US, Inc.) operating a mobile-first cross-border money transfer, digital payments, crypto, and investing platform across Africa and the diaspora. Founded in 2018 by Ham Serunjogi (Uganda) and Maijid Moujaled (Ghana) after they met at Grinnell College in Iowa, Chipper became one of Africa's fintech unicorns in 2021 and has raised over $340M to date. The consumer app — available on iOS, Android, and web — supports peer-to-peer and cross-border transfers across 21+ African countries, virtual Visa cards (Chipper Card), bill pay and airtime top-ups, fractional US-stock investing (Chipper Stocks, 6,000+ public companies, from $1), and historically crypto trading (BTC/ETH). Reported scale includes 5M+ registered users, 1M+ Visa cards issued, and 250,000+ daily transactions. Direct consumer markets include Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda, the UK, and the US. On the developer side, Chipper exposes the Chipper Network API ("Pay With Chipper") — a merchant-facing API that lets authorized businesses accept cross-border payments across 9 currencies, initiate payouts, issue refunds, and look up Chipper user accounts, authenticated with a Chipper User ID + Network API Key. Documentation is published as a Postman collection and access is gated by merchant onboarding; no public OpenAPI or open-source SDK is currently published. Adjacent products include Chipper ID (AI-led identity verification), Chipper Enterprise (bulk payments and collections), Business Accounts, and Zoona (agent-network remittances), plus an integration with TBD's tbDEX protocol for decentralized cross-border payments.

providers.name: Four Pillars
providers.description: Four Pillars is a research-driven blockchain enterprise headquartered in Asia, operating through three divisions: FP Research publishes primary analysis of crypto protocols, markets, and policy with deep regional expertise across Korea and the broader Asian market; FP Validated runs validator and node infrastructure across proof-of-stake networks, pairing research with live operations; and FP Institution advises banks, financial institutions, and corporates on blockchain strategy. The firm serves founders, funds, and regulators, and is a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. It is a research and advisory business rather than a developer-facing API platform, and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Prypco
providers.description: PRYPCO is a Dubai-based PropTech platform building an integrated real estate ecosystem for the United Arab Emirates. Its products include Blocks (fractional property investment starting from AED 500), Mint (blockchain-based tokenized real estate buying, selling, and trading, run in partnership with the Dubai Land Department), Mortgage (instant pre-approval and mortgage comparison), Golden Visa application assistance, a general property buy/sell/rent management service, and One (an agent platform with listing and commission tooling). PRYPCO Real Estate LLC is registered in Dubai, UAE. The company operates a consumer web and mobile product surface and publishes no public developer API; this profile is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network, surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and awaiting any future developer/API surface.

providers.name: Summoners Arena
providers.description: Summoners Arena is a blockchain-based, multi-genre play-to-earn game universe set in the antique lore of Summonia, where players summon, evolve, and battle NFT heroes across PvP modes (Arena, Battleground) and PvE content (Dungeon, Campaign), with an in-game NFT marketplace supporting hero renting, equipment collection, and forging. Backed by Pantera Capital, it operates in the Web3 / crypto gaming sector. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes a consumer game and community surface but no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or well-known discovery documents were found.

providers.name: Abaxx
providers.description: Abaxx Technologies is a financial software and market infrastructure company whose principal operating business, Abaxx Exchange, is a centrally-cleared commodity futures and derivatives exchange headquartered in Singapore and focused on energy-transition commodities across four markets: Energy (LNG), Environmental (carbon credits), Battery Materials (nickel, lithium), and Precious Metals. Abaxx Clearing (Abaxx Singapore Clearing Corporation) centrally clears the contracts, and the group also develops SMX (smart data / consensus-formation) technology. Trading runs on the markets.abaxx.exchange platform; market data is distributed to third parties including TradingView (ABAXX: symbol prefix), ipushpull (Microsoft Excel add-in) and LSEG/Refinitiv. Abaxx Technologies is publicly listed (Cboe Canada: ABXX; OTCQX: ABXXF). Abaxx does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI/FIX specification, SDKs or an MCP server; connectivity is arranged through member/broker onboarding. This profile originated as an earlybird portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network and has been enriched with verified public identity and security-posture signals.

providers.name: Bloom
providers.description: Bloom was a decentralized identity, credit-attestation and verifiable-credentials company backed by Pantera Capital, built on Ethereum and IPFS around three products: BloomID (identity attestation), BloomIQ (a credit registry) and BloomScore (credit risk scoring). Its stated aim was to let traditional and digital-currency lenders serve people who cannot obtain a bank account or a credit score, and it announced a TransUnion partnership in 2020 for consumer credit monitoring. Bloom is wound down. Its integration SDKs were archived on GitHub in 2021, its API, documentation and status hosts no longer resolve, bloom.co now redirects to a domain-broker sale listing, and Bloom HoldCo LLC filed a Form 15-12G on 2025-08-14 terminating Exchange Act registration of its BLT token with holders of record stated as "none". What survives is open source: 40 public repositories under github.com/hellobloom and 19 unmaintained but installable npm packages under the @bloomprotocol scope implementing the W3C and DIF decentralized-identity stack (Verifiable Credentials, DIDs, Presentation Exchange, Credential Manifest, WACI).

providers.name: Divine
providers.description: Divine Research Inc. is a fintech company building blockchain-based unsecured lending for underserved borrowers in emerging markets. Its flagship product, Credit, issues small stablecoin (USDC) loans that start small and can grow to $1,000 as borrowers build trust, with algorithmically set interest rates and default rates that have approached zero. Borrowers access loans through a World MiniApp, while liquidity providers supply capital and earn yield through the Credit Vault at credit.cash. As of late 2024 the platform had issued hundreds of thousands of loans to more than 500,000 borrowers. Divine is backed by Paradigm and was surfaced through its portfolio; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network. Divine currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Digital Currency Group
providers.description: Digital Currency Group (DCG) is a cryptocurrency and blockchain holding and venture company founded in 2015 by Barry Silbert and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut. DCG builds, incubates, and invests in companies across the digital asset ecosystem, including subsidiaries such as Grayscale Investments and Foundry. It operates as an investor and parent company rather than a direct API provider; this network profile tracks DCG's public web presence and corporate surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures. Sector: fintech / digital assets.

providers.name: enechain
providers.description: enechain operates the largest energy exchange in Japan, offering trading opportunities for wholesale electricity and environmental values across an over-the-counter marketplace that connects energy market participants. Headquartered in Tokyo, the company builds energy markets that help buyers and sellers discover prices, manage risk, and trade power and environmental-value products, under the mission "Building Energy Markets, Coloring Our Society." enechain was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures; it publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Royal
providers.description: Royal is a music-and-crypto company backed by a16z and Paradigm that originally let fans buy tokenized shares of songs (Limited Digital Assets, or LDAs) so they could earn streaming royalties alongside the artists they support. As of mid-2026 the public site at royal.io states the company is "reinventing itself" and is between products, keeping only its legal pages and LDA support live; it publishes no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or public API surface at this time. This profile tracks Royal as an API Evangelist network company and will be enriched further if and when a public API or developer program appears.

providers.name: Triumph Arcade
providers.description: Triumph Labs (originally Triumph Arcade) is a consumer entertainment and commerce company that builds mobile apps for competitive, skill-based gaming and collectibles. Its flagship products are Triumph: Play for Cash, a real-money skill-gaming platform, and Rips by Triumph, a live collectibles and trading-card ripping experience. Backed by Multicoin Capital, the company operates consumer iOS apps and publishes no public developer API surface; this profile tracks the company identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Media Chain
providers.description: Mediachain (Mediachain Labs) was a decentralized universal media library and attribution protocol built on IPFS and blockchain technology, designed to let creators and applications collaborate on open metadata about creative works and track the provenance and ownership of online images and other media. Founded in 2016 with seed funding from Andreessen Horowitz and Union Square Ventures, the company was acqui-hired by Spotify in April 2017 to help build fair, blockchain-based royalty attribution for rightsholders. The company is now defunct and its primary domain (mediachain.io) is a parked page, but its open-source protocol, design documentation, Protocol Buffer definitions, and first-party client libraries (the `aleph`/`mcclient` JavaScript client on npm and the `mediachain-client` Python reader on PyPI) remain public under the github.com/mediachain organization. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from its surviving open-source surface.

providers.name: 01 Exchange
providers.description: 01 Exchange (01.xyz) was a full-suite decentralized derivatives exchange on Solana, offering cross-margined and cross-collateralized Perpetual Futures and Power Perpetuals (SQUOL) built on a fully on-chain Serum limit orderbook, with support for up to 100 markets and 50 collateral tokens and up to 20x leverage. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The people and product behind 01 are now part of N1 (app.n1.xyz), where trading, points, and rewards have migrated. This profile captures 01 Exchange's historical developer surface: the TypeScript, Python, and Rust SDKs and on-chain program interface published by the Zero One Global Foundation (github.com/01protocol).

providers.name: Mangata Finance
providers.description: Mangata Finance (Mangata X, since rebranded GASP) is a decentralized exchange built as a Substrate parachain in the Polkadot and Kusama ecosystem. It is designed for algorithmic traders and DeFi frontends, offering gas-free swaps, an omnichain ZK-rollup architecture, and a Proof-of-Liquidity consensus model where liquidity providers help secure the network. There is no REST or OpenAPI surface; developers integrate through a TypeScript SDK (@mangata-finance/sdk) that communicates with the Mangata Substrate node over Polkadot.js JSON-RPC/WebSocket, with published type-definition packages and open-source node, bridge, and dev-kit repositories under the gasp-xyz GitHub organization.

providers.name: Teller Finance
providers.description: Teller Finance (Teller Protocol) is a decentralized, multi-chain lending and borrowing protocol on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, and BNB Chain. Borrowers take fixed-APR, time-based loans from isolated lending pools using their tokens as collateral, with no oracle-driven margin-call liquidations, through an open order-book of markets governed by the TellerV2 smart contract. The developer surface is on-chain (Solidity smart contracts) plus a GraphQL subgraph for read-side data and an embeddable Cash Advance widget (npm) that any dapp can drop into its front end - there is no hosted REST API, OAuth server, or API-key program; authentication is wallet-based. Teller was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched here from its public developer surface.

providers.name: CoinTracker
providers.description: CoinTracker is a cryptocurrency portfolio tracker and crypto tax software that connects a user's exchange accounts and blockchain wallets to automatically track holdings, calculate cost basis and capital gains, and generate tax reports and IRS forms. It supports a large catalog of exchanges, wallets, and cryptocurrencies, and offers tax-loss harvesting, performance tracking, and integrations with consumer tax-filing products. For developers and partners, CoinTracker publishes a first-party JavaScript SDK (@cointracker/tax-kit) for supplying cost-basis data; its core HTTP API is offered through enterprise and partner integrations rather than a self-serve public developer program. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from publicly discoverable surfaces (npm, GitHub, status page, DNS/TLS).

providers.name: Meso
providers.description: Meso is payment infrastructure designed for crypto. Backed by Ribbit Capital, the company is positioned as a payments-rails provider for the cryptocurrency sector. As of this enrichment pass its public web presence is a single-page marketing site at meso.network with no publicly documented developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition surfaced yet. The one machine-readable artifact the company publishes is a PGP-signed RFC 9116 security.txt at /.well-known/security.txt declaring a security contact and disclosure policy. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Ribbit Capital portfolio lead and is tracked for future API surface as the product launches.

providers.name: Noox
providers.description: Noox is a Web3 platform for creating and collecting achievement badges as soulbound NFTs, letting people build verifiable on-chain reputation. Users discover community-curated Web3 achievements, check eligibility, and mint them as identity-bound (non-transferable) NFTs, while creators build custom on-chain achievements from live blockchain data with a no-code, template-based designer. The protocol is deployed on Ethereum mainnet (badge, badgeMinter and feeCollector smart contracts) and is powered by Alchemy Web3 infrastructure. Noox is a portfolio company of Electric Capital in the crypto sector. Note: Noox exposes no public REST/HTTP developer API, OpenAPI, GraphQL/subgraph, or SDK; its developer surface is the on-chain smart contracts.

providers.name: Azra Games
providers.description: Azra Games is a mobile role-playing game studio founded in 2022 by Mark Otero and headquartered in Sacramento, California. The studio builds RPGs on its proprietary "RPG GameKit" technology, with its flagship title UnGodly, a dark sword-and-sorcery RPG. Azra Games is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a game studio it publishes a public website, news, careers, terms, and privacy pages but does not expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Shibuya
providers.description: Shibuya is a platform for curated short films and the independent creators behind them, describing itself as a home where fans help greenlight the future of film and audiences discover original storytelling. Operated by NotShibuya, Inc. and backed by a16z, Shibuya began as a web3 storytelling experiment and has grown into a community-driven curation platform for short-form film, winning a 2025 Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Innovation in Emerging Media Programming. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Shibuya publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its real public web properties.

providers.name: Slingshot
providers.description: Slingshot is a self-custody, multi-chain DeFi application and wallet founded in 2020 and headquartered in San Francisco, letting retail users search, send, receive, and swap tens of thousands of cryptocurrencies at aggregated best prices with 0% swap fees. It is available on Web, iOS, and Android with bridging support across Ethereum Mainnet, Arbitrum, Arbitrum Nova, Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, and Canto. Backed by Electric Capital, Slingshot combined centralized-exchange ease with the openness of decentralized exchanges. NOTE: Slingshot announced it is sunsetting, advising users to export their private keys before February 28, 2026; its GitHub organization was archived in January 2026. This profile documents a consumer DeFi product that exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Ampleforth
providers.description: Ampleforth is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol behind AMPL, a price-stable but supply-elastic cryptocurrency that targets the CPI-adjusted 2019 US dollar by algorithmically adjusting token supply (rebasing) across all holders rather than moving price. The ecosystem spans the AMPL rebasing token, Wrapped AMPL (WAMPL), the FORTH governance token and DAO, and the SPOT inflation-resistant store-of-value protocol built on tranched AMPL collateral. Ampleforth is open-source (smart contracts under the fragmentsorg GitHub organization, working name uFragments), audited, and deployed on Ethereum with cross-chain support. Surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and enriched in the API Evangelist network from its public docs, GitHub org, blog, and community channels; it publishes protocol documentation and an llms.txt but no REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Basel III
providers.description: Basel III is a comprehensive global regulatory framework developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) in response to the 2007-2008 financial crisis. It strengthens bank capital requirements by requiring higher quality and quantity of capital (CET1, Tier 1, Total Capital), introduces new liquidity standards (LCR and NSFR), adds a leverage ratio backstop, and includes countercyclical capital buffers and G-SIB surcharges. Basel III implementation in the EU/UK is delivered via CRD IV/V and CRR regulations. The final Basel III package (sometimes called Basel IV) addresses output floor and credit risk model constraints introduced in 2017.

providers.name: Blur
providers.description: Blur is a New York-based NFT marketplace and aggregator built for professional traders on Ethereum, founded by the pseudonymous "Pacman" (Tieshun Roquerre) in October 2022 and backed by Paradigm and Standard Crypto. The flagship product, blur.io, offers zero marketplace fees, multi-marketplace sweeping, bulk listing/bidding, real-time mempool reveal sniping, and a portfolio-grade analytics surface that aggregates liquidity from OpenSea, X2Y2, LooksRare, and other Seaport-compatible venues. Blur also operates Blend, a peer-to-peer perpetual NFT lending protocol designed by Paradigm researchers that powers ETH-against-NFT borrowing and Buy-Now-Pay-Later flows without oracles or fixed expiries — Blend has captured the dominant share of NFT lending volume on Ethereum. The BLUR token, distributed via multi-season airdrop campaigns, governs the Blur DAO through the Blur Foundation. The same team launched Blast, an Ethereum L2 with native yield, which now hosts its own NFT activity. Blur does not publish an official public developer API or SDK; on-chain integration happens via the deployed marketplace and Blend smart contracts (Seaport-compatible), and marketplace data is reached through third-party indexers such as Bitquery, SimpleHash, and Alchemy rather than a Blur-operated REST or GraphQL endpoint.

providers.name: PartyDAO
providers.description: PartyDAO is the decentralized autonomous organization behind Party Protocol, an open, GPL-3.0 protocol for on-chain group coordination that aims to make Ethereum "multiplayer." Party Protocol lets groups form a Party (a shared Ethereum account with members, an inventory, and governance), collectively crowdfund to acquire assets, govern shared holdings, and distribute value to members — all through audited Solidity smart contracts rather than a hosted HTTP API. PartyDAO also ships Party (party.app), a consumer application built on the protocol. The developer surface is entirely on-chain: smart contracts, deployed contract addresses, and technical documentation for integrating via web3 libraries and direct contract calls. There is no REST/HTTP API, hosted SDK, or OAuth surface; integration happens by calling the deployed contracts.

providers.name: Sentient
providers.description: Sentient (Sentient Labs / Sentient Foundation) is an open-source AI research lab and crypto protocol building Open, Monetizable, and Loyal (OML) artificial general intelligence. Its work spans agent frameworks (ROMA recursive meta-agent, Open Deep Search, EvoSkill agent-skill synthesis), the OML 1.0 model-fingerprinting system for verifiable model ownership and monetization, and the GRID protocol with Sentient Chat as a universal interface for discovering, composing, and coordinating AI artifacts. Backed by Pantera Capital, Sentient publishes peer-reviewed research (NeurIPS, ICML, COLM) and ships its tooling as open-source repositories on GitHub and models on Hugging Face rather than as a hosted commercial REST API.

providers.name: Sturdy
providers.description: Sturdy is a decentralized liquid money market protocol for on-chain lending and borrowing. Sturdy V2 uses a two-tier architecture: a base layer of risk-isolated lending pairs, where each siloed market consists of a single lending asset and a single collateral asset, and an aggregation layer on top that lets lenders choose acceptable collateral types while avoiding liquidity fragmentation. The protocol is oracle-agnostic (using RedStone, API3, and eOracle feeds depending on the market), is governed by the $STRDY token and the Sturdy DAO, and has been audited by Zellic, ChainSecurity, Spearbit, Certik, Code4rena, and Quantstamp. Sturdy is an on-chain smart-contract protocol rather than a hosted REST API: its developer surface is the published smart contracts, oracle integrations, and the Sturdy Subnet, with no first-party web API, SDK, or OpenAPI. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Brine (Tanx)
providers.description: Brine — now rebranded as tanX — is a cross-chain, self-custodial orderbook decentralized exchange (DEX) built on StarkWare's StarkEx Layer-2 scaling engine. It combines the trustless, non-custodial security of a DEX with the speed and low fees of a centralized exchange: gasless trading, rapid off-chain order execution with on-chain settlement, cross-chain deposits and withdrawals, and simple APIs for programmatic trading. The company is backed by Pantera Capital and is repositioning around "a secure and compliant future for crypto." This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Pantera Capital's portfolio and enriched by the pipeline; as of this pass the public REST API host is no longer reachable and the developer surface is limited to the GitBook documentation.

providers.name: Wintermute
providers.description: Wintermute is a leading global algorithmic trading firm and cryptocurrency market maker providing institutional-grade liquidity across centralized exchanges, decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols, and over-the-counter (OTC) markets. Its offerings span OTC spot trading for hundreds of tokens, options with bespoke structures, forwards, CFDs, programmatic "API liquidity", and a DeFi trading and liquidity-provisioning arm, plus Wintermute Ventures, an early-stage investment vehicle. Access to Wintermute's trading services is institutional and onboarding-gated through the node.wintermute.com portal (authenticated via an Auth0-backed OIDC / OAuth2 identity provider); there is no public self-serve developer API or open OpenAPI at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Alliance DAO
providers.description: Alliance (Alliance DAO) is a leading crypto, fintech, and AI startup accelerator. Its cohort-based program pairs two weeks of in-person onboarding in New York City with eight weeks of remote acceleration, offering mentorship, lectures, weekly check-ins, and a Demo Day pitch event. Alliance invests $500,000 per startup and runs three cohorts per year. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital, Alliance publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: DCG
providers.description: Digital Currency Group (DCG) is a crypto-industry venture and holding company that describes itself as the enduring investor and operator of the crypto industry. Investing in digital currencies and blockchain since 2012, DCG has built a portfolio of 200+ equity investments, 50+ fund investments, and 30+ token and digital-asset positions across 25+ countries. It owns and operates category-leading subsidiaries including Grayscale (crypto asset management), Foundry (mining and staking infrastructure), CoinDesk (media, data and events), Genesis (institutional financial services), Luno (consumer wallet), HQ, and TradeBlock. DCG is a corporate holding and investment company and does not publish a public developer API; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead.

providers.name: Everyrealm
providers.description: Everyrealm Inc. is a Web3 and metaverse company building virtual communities inside in-game worlds, positioned at the intersection of gaming, entertainment, and blockchain technology. Under the banner "Connecting what matters," Everyrealm develops immersive, gamified virtual worlds and experiences, partners with gaming platforms, and invests across the broader metaverse and digital-real-estate ecosystem. The company has raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Coinbase Ventures, Brevan Howard, Hashed, and other prominent investors. Everyrealm is a consumer- and community-facing operator rather than an API-first developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or programmatic API surface. This entry was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and has been enriched with public identity, legal, and domain-security signals.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.
